name: Avail
label: Lookout!
lede: [[Joe Banks]] moved a Reston hardcore band into a Richmond rowhouse, put the drummer on the microphone, and spent a decade writing Richmond into the song titles. The band quit in 2007 without announcing it, then sold out The National in about ten seconds in 2019.

eras.title: Out of Reston, into a rowhouse
eras.text: Avail started as a suburban hardcore band in Reston, Virginia, in the long shadow of D.C. Around 1990 Banks gave up on the D.C. area and moved the band into a Richmond rowhouse, and drummer Tim Barry took over the singing.

years.h: Avail starts in the Northern Virginia suburbs
years.p: Banks plays guitar, Brien Stewart sings, Doug Crosby drums and Mikey Warstler plays bass. Banks is the only one of the four still in the band.

years.src: Wikipedia: Who's to Say What Stays the Same · Fat Wreck Chords
years.h: A drummer from a rival band sits in at Inner Ear
years.p: For Avail's first vinyl session in December 1989 at Inner Ear Studio, Stewart sings, Banks plays guitar and D.J. Grimes plays bass. Barry, formerly of Learning Disabled Kids, takes the drums.
years.xp:
The four songs first came out on the 1990 cassette Reaching Out, then as the Who's to Say What Stays the Same EP on SunSpot Records in May 1991, Avail's first vinyl. Banks produced it.

Wikipedia credits Barry with drums on the session. Fat Wreck Chords' band bio says he joined as the drummer and moved to the microphone around 1990.

years.h: Banks gives up on D.C. and rents a Richmond rowhouse
years.p: Banks relocates the band to Richmond in 1990, and Barry moves from the drum stool to the microphone. From then on, Richmond is what the songs are about.
years.xp:
Fat Wreck Chords' bio says the band gave up on the D.C. area in 1990 and took a historic Richmond rowhouse to get serious. By 2003, Barry told Razorcake, Avail had practiced in Banks's house for nine years, and Banks had since bought it.

Barry said the neighbors, a hair shop, a flower shop and bar owners among them, were told up front that the band practiced there and the room was soundproofed.

eras.title: Learning to tour, then Lookout!
eras.text: Avail learned to tour from a borrowed phone list and landed on Lookout! Records, the Berkeley label that had put out Green Day's first records. Two Lookout! albums, cut in a Silver Spring, Maryland studio, put Richmond on the map for punks everywhere else.

years.src: Wikipedia: Satiate · Discogs · Razorcake #14 · Wikipedia: Live at the Kings Head Inn
years.h: Satiate starts on Catheter-Assembly and ends up on Lookout!
years.p: Adam Thompson's Catheter-Assembly label puts out the debut, then Old Glory, then Lookout! on CD in 1994. The song Mr. Morgan is about an elderly Richmond man killed in a robbery.
years.xp:
Tracked in September and October 1991 at Gizmo and Wolftrack studios with Chuck McCauley on bass and [[Erik Larson|d29befcc-6291-46c9-873e-bf477f0de6b6]] on drums. The credits list Beau Beau as Cheerleader, his job title ever since.

Lookout!'s 1994 CD added two songs from the 1993 Attempt to Regress 7-inch. That same year Old Glory put out Live at the Kings Head Inn, taped in Norfolk, Virginia, in April 1993.

years.h: A phone list from Born Against's Adam Nathanson becomes a tour
years.p: Nathanson mails Barry the numbers from [[Born Against|983825cd-4c25-45c5-adbb-3f9cdced6285]]'s own tours, and Avail books its first real tour from them.
years.xp:
Before that, Barry told Razorcake, Avail had played two out-of-state shows and called it a tour. Nathanson, he said, "sat me down and taught me how to set up tours."

Years later the band was booking tours of 160 dates.

years.h: Avail covers John Mellencamp on Dixie
years.p: Recorded in June 1994 with Larry Packer at Uncle Punchy Studios in Silver Spring, Maryland: twelve originals plus Pink Houses.
years.xp: The line-up was Barry, Banks, McCauley, Larson and Beau Beau. Barry has named Springsteen and Mellencamp as models for writing about everyday life until it turns political.

years.cap: Flyer for Avail, Young Pioneers and Endeavor at Wetlands, New York, Sunday April 3, c. 1994
years.h: Barry plays bass in a second band, (Young) Pioneers
years.p: From 1994 to 1995 Barry also plays bass in the Richmond folk-punk band [[(Young) Pioneers|642ef2de-0d93-45aa-a27c-a93f32ebfbbb]], who share the 1997 Lookout! split The Fall of Richmond with Avail.

yt: Live at the Emerson Theater, November 17, 1996
years.h: News of Bob Baynor's death reaches Avail at 4 a.m. on a Friday
years.p: Baynor played bass in [[Maximillian Colby|ed0c2410-784d-489e-864e-17c3ebeffd7d]] and died in 1995. Avail named its third album for that hour, and F.C.A. is the tribute to him.
years.xp:
Baynor played bass in Maximillian Colby, a band formed at James Madison University in Harrisonburg, Virginia; Lovitt Records says his death in 1995 brought that band to a halt. No source found gives a cause.

Recorded January to February 1996 at Uncle Punchy with Rob Kelshian on bass. One track was sung by Ben Winkler, the sleeve says, at a rest stop off the New Jersey Turnpike. Simple Song later landed on Tony Hawk's Pro Skater 4.

eras.title: The bassist from the laundromat
eras.text: After a bassist quit on a European tour, a man from a laundromat took his place, and Avail made Over the James, which Decibel later called a melodic hardcore classic. Then came Fat Wreck Chords, a muralist on drums, and tours long enough that the band lived a third of each year in a van.

years.h: Gwomper turns up in a laundromat with his clothes in a trash bag
years.p: After a bassist quits on a European tour, Barry finds Justin "Gwomper" Burdick sitting in a Richmond laundromat. Gwomper has never played bass.
years.xp:
Barry handed him a classical guitar and told him to learn all the Avail songs while the band toured Europe for five weeks; he switched to bass when it came home. Gwomper told Decibel he had been saving for a winter in Colorado, lost the money, and came back to Richmond instead.

He credits Chuck McCauley, who played bass on Satiate and Dixie, for teaching him the parts.

years.src: Wikipedia: Over the James · Decibel · Pitchfork
years.h: Over the James puts Lombardy St. and Scuffle Town on a record
years.p: Cut in December 1997 at Montana Studio in Richmond, Avail's fourth album has Gwomper on bass. Pitchfork called it the apotheosis of the band's sound.
years.xp:
The line-up was Barry, Banks, Gwomper, Larson and Beau Beau on backing vocals. Banks built the intro of Deepwood on a Boss drum machine, writing the lick on bass before moving it to guitar.

Barry told Decibel that hardcore kids, leftist political fans and pop-punk crowds all started turning up at the same Avail shows. Pitchfork's Zach Baron gave it 7.7. In May 2019 Decibel inducted it into its Hall of Fame as a melodic hardcore classic.

years.h: Richmond muralist Ed Trask takes the drums for One Wrench
years.p: Avail's first album for Fat Wreck Chords was recorded in March 2000 at Montana Studio in Richmond with Mark Miley. The Pittsburgh Post-Gazette called the band undersung working-class heroes.
years.xp: Avail's Fat run began with the 100 Times EP in 1999. [[Ed Trask|0cf5525b-a45c-4e1d-b269-d306b793d442]], a 1992 VCU painting graduate, kept painting illegal murals on tour and became one of Richmond's best-known muralists. Larson, Avail's drummer since Satiate, went on to Alabama Thunderpussy.

years.big: "I have no idea what Beau does but he does everything."
years.src: Decibel · Vice: Avail Hype · Punknews · Discogs · Razorcake #14
years.h: Shirtless and often missing a tooth, Beau Beau Butler works the pit
years.p: Barry's line on his friend since kindergarten, Avail's cheerleader. Butler plays no instrument; he stage-dives, sings backup and has broken bones and chipped teeth in the crowd.
years.xp:
Barry told Decibel that Beau started out sitting beside the drum riser and simply began stage diving; nobody gave him the job. Barry calls him critic, fifth songwriter and crowd motivator. He is credited as Cheerleader on Satiate as early as 1991.

Asked by Punknews, Avail said Barry and Beau had been hurt in the crowd and on stage more times than they could count: cuts, broken bones, chipped teeth, stitches. Razorcake's version of the job: get the crowd dancing and be something to look at.

years.src: Wikipedia: Front Porch Stories · Fat Wreck Chords · Riot Fest
years.h: Front Porch Stories, the last Avail album so far
years.p: Cut in June 2002 at Sound of Music in Richmond with producer Bryan Paulson and released on Fat. Its motto, Ride fast, live slow, is one Barry still uses.
years.xp: Fat's bio from this period says Avail spent about a third of each year jammed in a van. Around the same time Simple Song, from 4am Friday, turned up on the Tony Hawk's Pro Skater 4 soundtrack.

eras.title: Food Not Bombs, freight trains and a quiet exit
eras.text: Avail was a working band giving its hometown money away, while Tim Barry rode freight trains and started singing alone with an acoustic guitar. Jade Tree reissued the Lookout! albums in 2006, no new album came, and in 2007 the band simply stopped.

years.h: Every dollar from Avail's Richmond shows goes to Food Not Bombs
years.p: Barry told Razorcake the band gave all its Richmond proceeds to the local chapter, which he had seen start a decade earlier. "It's a substantial amount of money every year," he said.
years.xp:
Barry said the money covered lawyer fees for arrests, kitchen equipment and cleaning supplies for running a real kitchen.

In the same interview he described riding freight out of Richmond's ACCA yard, a habit learned from a friend he called Ronny Richmond. He called it voluntary homelessness, and said it fed his songs.

years.h: Barry picks up an acoustic guitar and plays alone
years.p: Barry began performing acoustic folk on his own in 2004, which led to Rivanna Junction on Chunksaah in 2006 and a solo catalog that outlasted Avail's first run.

years.cap: Beau Beau Butler doing his cheerleader routine during Avail's set at Fest 6, Gainesville, Florida, September 2007
q: I wasn't having any fun. There was too much tension in the van.
years.h: Avail stops without announcing it
years.p: Barry later told Vice the fun was gone and the van was tense. The last tour paid each member $250 for ten days.
years.xp:
Everyone was working several jobs. A New York fan named Pete, who had seen every Avail show in the city since ABC No Rio, told Barry he could tell something was wrong at the final Knitting Factory show.

Barry told RVA Magazine in 2019 there were not many layers to it: playing just was not as fun as it once was. During the break Banks and others played in Freeman.

eras.title: Back at The National
eras.text: Twelve years after the last show, The National in Richmond sold out in seconds. A second night followed, then a Decibel Hall of Fame nod, dates with Hot Water Music and a Satiate reissue.

years.h: Beau Butler tells Vice he'll run for mayor of Richmond
years.p: Avail's hype man promises $2 highballs, a ban on Crocs and flip-flops, and a website shaming bad tippers. The run is for 2016.

years.cap: Barry, Banks, Gwomper, Larson and Beau Beau Butler, c. 2019
years.h: One reunion show sells out in about ten seconds, so there's a second
years.p: Barry agrees after listening to Over the James with his daughters around its 20th anniversary. The July 19 date at The National goes in about ten seconds; July 20 follows.
years.xp:
Barry told Butler he would play if "all I had to do was write the setlist and sing." Butler passed it on to the others. Iron Reagan quietly lent the band practice space, and Barry showed up to the first practice without warming up. He told Vice: "There was not even much talking. They just started."

The National holds about 1,500. Tickets for the second night were sold in person at the venue, and Barry drove past with his daughters to see the line. They sold out within hours.

years.cap: Avail at The National, Richmond, July 19, 2019
years.h: Avail opens at The National with South Bound 95
years.p: Barry, Banks, Gwomper, Larson and Beau Beau Butler play together for the first time in 12 years. Butler brings foam fingers, Super Soakers and a novelty cowboy hat.
years.xp: Stereogum's Tom Breihan reported a crowd mostly in its forties and fifties and a band playing with full intensity. A few songs in, Barry told the room it felt good.

years.h: Avail reissues Satiate itself and hits the road with Hot Water Music
years.p: The first Satiate vinyl in about 15 years, for the debut's 30th anniversary. Dates in Carrboro, Atlanta and St. Petersburg follow.
